title: Fragment Hash ACK and Idempotent Reassembly Protocol for SSE + FunctionCall Boundary Guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a robust SSE fragment-level acknowledgement and idempotent reassembly protocol that preserves function/tool-call and structured-output atomicity across client reconnects. This ticket addresses cases where clients disconnect mid-stream, server rotates shards, or intermediary proxies drop frames, and ensures callers observing a resumed stream see a consistent, non-duplicated ordered sequence with clear cutover when function/tool call frames must be delivered atomically.
decision_log: Use a content-addressed fragment identifier: SHA256(prefix + sequence_no + optional-batch-id) to detect duplicate fragments on reconnect and avoid reapplying deltas.
Keep server-side fragment retention window configurable (default: 10 minutes) to balance memory usage and resume reliability.

Guarantee function/tool-call atomicity by marking the first fragment of a function call with a boundary flag and require resume handshake to include last-observed-fragment-id; server will replay whole function-call from its start if resume token is older than that boundary.
Opted for a lightweight resumable handshake over existing SSE headers to maintain compatibility with legacy clients; introduce optional Resume-Token header and Resume-Mode query param.
Emit provenance metadata per fragment (fragment-id, prev-fragment-id, cumulative-checksum) for post-mortem and debugging in Console traces.
Do not require client ACKs per-fragment by default; support optional client ACK mode for high-cost tooling integrations (enabled per-route).
Fallback policy: if server cannot reconcile resume token, fall back to a coherent server-supplied partial snapshot event and a restart-of-stream marker to avoid silent truncation.
Security: ensure resume tokens are short-lived and tied to connection/session; mark security_review_required = true for KMS rotation review for tokens stored in logs.
Compatibility: provide a shim that maps an older resume-token format (numeric offsets) to new fragment-id based resume semantics during a transition window.

Performance trade-off: small fragments (<=1KB) simplify reassembly and reduce duplicated retransmission cost at the expense of slightly higher per-fragment overhead; we default to 2KB fragment target and allow adaptive sizing based on latency SLOs.

acceptance_criteria: SSE clients that disconnect and reconnect with a valid resume token do not receive duplicate fragments (no duplicate content visible to application layer) in 99.9% of simulated reconnect scenarios.

Function/tool-call boundaries are preserved: a resumed stream that intersects a function-call boundary will either replay the whole function-call from its start or present a server-supplied coherent snapshot; partial function-call fragments must not be delivered to the application.
Console shows fragment-level trace links (fragment-id) and stream resume/restart markers for at least 30 days in dev/staging clusters.
Server-side retention config default is 10 minutes; end-to-end tests validate retention eviction behavior and fallback snapshot semantics.
No regression in baseline latency SLOs for non-resumed streams (<=5% p99 increase in controlled load tests).
Docs and SDK shims published: Node and Python SDKs expose Resume-Token negotiation and optional ACK mode.
test_plan: Unit tests for fragment-id generation, collision resistance (statistical), and reassembly logic.
Integration tests: orchestrate client disconnects at varying points (before/inside/after function-call) and assert atomicity guarantees.
Chaos tests: simulate proxy dropping frames, out-of-order delivery, and server-side shard failover during streaming with resume enabled.
Performance tests: run k6 scenarios at 1k/5k/10k concurrent streaming clients to measure retention memory and p99 latency impact.
Compatibility tests: run legacy client with numeric-offset resume-token and verify shim translation and correct resume behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy to runtime canary cluster (us-east-1-canary) with retention window=2m and per-route resume disabled by default. Monitor retention_hits, resume_success_rate, and stream_restart_rate.
Phase 2 (staged): Enable for 10% of production traffic and enable fragment telemetry in Console. SDKs released in minor version with opt-in docs.
Phase 3 (full): Default resume enabled for all hosted routes; increase retention default to 10m. Publish migration doc and compatibility notes for on-prem customers.
Rollback: If resume_success_rate < 99% or stream_restart_rate > 0.5% above baseline for 30m, rollback the canary and revert feature flag.
